newsitem.title: USA: Ford total U.S. vehicle sales down 4.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Ford total U.S. vehicle sales down 4.4 pct.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Monday total vehicle sales declined 4.4 percent in the month of April, with U.S. sales of North American built cars at 126,906, down 10.1 percent from April 1996.
Light truck sales rose 0.6 percent to 188,217, up from 187,034 in the year ago period, Ford said.
Total vehicle sales were 322,243, down from 336,933 a year ago.

The nation's second largest auto maker also said it was adding 10,000 more trucks to its second quarter North American production plans, bringing the total to 750,000 and up 11 percent from second quarter 1996.

"Our dealers could have delivered even more trucks to their customers in April were it not for a shortage of bi-level rail cars to transport new trucks," Bob Rewey, Ford's group vice president of marketing and sales, said in a news release. He said the problem impacted availability of its Windstar minivan and to a lesser extent its F-Series pickup trucks and Explorer sport/utility vehicle.
Ford also said it has already received more than 9,000 dealer orders for its Lincoln-Mercury Navigator sport/utility vehicle, which will go into production next week.
Total sport/utility sales in April were 52,611, up 38 percent from 37,997 a year ago, Ford said.
Imported car sales, excluding Ford's Jaguar unit, were 3,269 in the month, down 27.8 percent from 4,529 a year ago.
Heavy truck sales were 3,851, down 7.3 percent from 4,156 a year ago.
Ford shares were up 1/8 at 34-7/8 Monday.
